name: Phthalocyanine Blue Pigments
scope: Global phthalocyanine (Pc) pigment demand is entering a fresh growth phase -- IndexBox projects roughly 5% CAGR to 2035, with electronics/optical uses (colour filters, conductive inks, precision manufacturing needing high-purity PB 15:6 / stabilised PB 15:4 grades) the fastest-growing segment, rising from about 15-18% to 22-25% of demand by 2035, alongside continued growth in the larger printing-ink/coatings/plastics base. This is not a from-scratch India opportunity -- Meghmani Organics already claims roughly 14% global market share and top-3 global capacity -- the open question is which listed Indian makers are actually positioned for the higher-value electronics-grade share of the growth versus only the traditional industrial end-use.
questions: What is phthalocyanine (Pc) blue/green pigment, how is copper phthalocyanine made, and why does the electronics/optical segment need a different, higher-purity grade (PB 15:6, stabilised PB 15:4) than standard ink, coating or plastics-grade material?

How large and how fast is global phthalocyanine pigment demand growing (IndexBox and other market-research estimates), and specifically how much faster is the electronics/optical end-use segment growing than the traditional inks/coatings/plastics base?

What is India's existing phthalocyanine manufacturing base and global standing today (capacity, market share, export orientation) -- which listed companies actually make phthalocyanine-type pigments, as opposed to other pigment or dye chemistries entirely?

For each listed company: what phthalocyanine-specific products, capacity and recent or planned capex do they have, and is there any stated move toward higher-purity electronics-grade output specifically, or is their exposure only to the traditional industrial end-use?
How much of this is already known or priced in: analyst and media coverage of these stocks tied specifically to pigments, and share-price performance over the last 6-12 months?

What are the risks: exposure to volatile input costs (copper, phthalic anhydride, phthalic-based intermediates), Chinese competition and pricing, customer concentration, and whether the electronics-grade opportunity is real current revenue or still aspirational?

What are the near-term catalysts and things to watch: capacity commissioning or expansion, new product qualifications for electronics-grade material, and quarterly results commentary on the pigments segment specifically?

phthalocyanine_makers: Indian listed manufacturers of phthalocyanine blue/green pigments
